create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows when acting as a SAML identity provider/broker entrypoint.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are expected and should not be flagged as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error StatusCode.
saml.note: Tests must inspect protocol-level outcome, not just HTTP status.

saml.description: ZITADEL commonly issues opaque access tokens instead of JWT access tokens by default.
saml.note: Do not flag non-JWT access tokens as malformed or missing claims; use introspection/userinfo.

saml.description: SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error status.
saml.note: Do not treat HTTP 200 alone as successful authentication for SAML tests.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, the returned token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows the documented RFC 8693 behavior in ZITADEL.

saml.description: Token introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: A false result from a non-audience client is expected and not evidence the token itself is invalid.

saml.description: ZITADEL issues opaque access tokens by default unless JWT access tokens are explicitly configured/requested.
saml.note: Lack of locally parseable JWT claims is by design and verification should use introspection or userinfo.

saml.description: Organization-specific login settings and IdP selection require the organization scope in the auth request when defaults are overridden.
saml.note: Different behavior with and without org scope can be expected configuration scoping, not cross-tenant confusion.

saml.description: ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default rather than JWT access tokens.
saml.note: Failure to locally decode an access token is expected and not a bug.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the brokered login through the OIDC authorization flow first and then submit the SAMLResponse to the external IdP callback with a matching flow state/InResponseTo. IdP-initiated SAML tests against ZITADEL are invalid and will fail by design.

For SAML broker tests, use POST form submission to the callback and include both SAMLResponse and RelayState. ZITADEL's SAML broker flow depends on prior flow initialization; sending a fabricated callback without first starting the flow will be rejected for the wrong reason.

The SAML IdP endpoint /saml/v2/SSO always returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; failures are encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT use raw HTTP status from that endpoint as the oracle for SAML success/failure. For broker tests, judge success by whether the downstream OIDC flow completes and token exchange/userinfo succeed.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure a SAML provider with explicit metadata/entity information first. If issuer trust is not fully configured from metadata, an issuer-mismatch result may reflect incomplete setup rather than a validation bypass.

For I1 signature-substitution and unsigned-assertion tests, ZITADEL as broker consumes SAML from an external IdP configured via metadata/certificate. The fuzzer MUST ensure the provider is created from attacker-controlled metadata when testing trust-anchor handling, and MUST distinguish broker acceptance from downstream OIDC completion. A failed downstream code exchange does not prove SAML signature validation worked.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, saml_assertion_id_replay, and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, include a CONTROL broker login with a valid assertion in the same provider configuration before the attack login. Without a control, callback failure cannot be distinguished from broken provider setup, missing login-policy enablement, or missing attribute-mapping actions.

ZITADEL user creation from external SAML IdPs may fail unless required user fields are mapped from IdP attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. For any test expecting first-login account creation, the fuzzer MUST provision attribute-mapping actions or use an already-linkable account; otherwise login failure is expected and not a security signal.

External IdP login must be enabled in the login policy (default or organization-specific). The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' for the relevant scope before any SAML broker login test, or failures are by configuration, not by security enforcement.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may not select the intended organization-specific SAML provider or login policy. Cross-org tests without this scope can produce false negatives or false positives.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces organization membership. For multi-tenant and cross-org tests, the fuzzer MUST treat this as exact-value semantics on the organization ID embedded in the scope string; it is not a wildcardable pattern. To vary organizations across attempts, generate distinct exact scopes per org rather than reusing a wildcard placeholder.

Token exchange audience is narrowing-only: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 audience-escalation tests, a rejection is by design when requesting a new audience not already present upstream. The fuzzer should only flag success of such an exchange as a violation, not rejection.

Token exchange scope may differ from the input token and can be extended or decreased by request, but invalid or excessive scope yields invalid_scope. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against upstream authorization and broker policy; do not assume requesting a broader scope should always succeed or always fail without checking the response scope.
The token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource-based audience tests on ZITADEL; use the audience parameter instead.

When requested_token_type=id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that access_token value as a bearer session token for subsequent API calls; use exchanges requesting an access token or JWT plus openid scope when a usable bearer token is needed.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving token exchange, an expired subject ID token rejection is by design and should not be interpreted as a broader replay defense beyond documented token validation.

JWT client assertions used for token or introspection authentication MUST have aud including ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat not older than 1 hour. For tests using private_key_jwt, failures outside this window are setup errors, not security findings. Use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} or shorter.

There is a numeric sentinel on JWT client assertion freshness: iat older than 1 hour is invalid. Never assume large negative skew is tolerated. Use current-time templates rather than hardcoded stale timestamps.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. For I5 audience-binding tests, introspection failure from a non-audience client is by design and should not be treated as token invalidity in general.

UserInfo requires an access token of a user, not a client token. The fuzzer MUST use the user access_token as session_token for verify_granted_identity; client_credentials or non-user tokens will fail by design.

ZITADEL may issue opaque access tokens by default. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume local JWT parsing of session_token will work; use userinfo or introspection for verification. A non-JWT access token is by design, not a malformed token bug.

For SAML MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, compare the same user under the same application/login policy context. Organization-specific login policy and external IdP enablement can change behavior legitimately; a valid bypass test must show SAML path skipping MFA where password path in the same context requires it.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow first and obtain a valid SAML request / request ID before attempting saml_login. IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform and will fail by design.

For SAML broker tests, the effective login result is usually completed through OIDC endpoints after brokering. The fuzzer MUST include start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token around SAML scenarios, because ZITADEL issues OIDC/OAuth tokens to the application after external IdP authentication.

SAML SSO endpoint errors are returned with HTTP 200 and encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message instead of HTTP 4xx/5xx. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from SAML endpoints as success by itself; it must inspect downstream flow completion or SAML status content to distinguish acceptance from rejection.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, ZITADEL documentation states SAML assertions/signatures must be validated by the SP and exchanged via metadata/certificates. The fuzzer MUST test acceptance/rejection by whether the brokered login completes, not by raw ACS HTTP status alone.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, include a control successful SAML login first, then replay the same assertion/request context. Without a control, a failed replay attempt cannot be distinguished from broken setup because ZITADEL only supports SP-initiated SAML and requires valid request context.

For I2 expired assertion tests, the fuzzer MUST run a control login with a valid assertion in the same provider/app setup before sending the expired assertion. Otherwise a failed login may be caused by missing attribute mapping, disabled external IdP login policy, or incomplete provider setup rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

External IdP login must be enabled in the login policy, either default or organization-specific. The fuzzer MUST ensure external login is allowed before any SAML broker login test, otherwise failures are configuration failures, not security rejections.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the fuzzer MUST send the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} in the authorization request to exercise the intended org-specific SAML provider and policy. Omitting it can route the test through default settings and invalidate tenant-isolation conclusions.

ZITADEL user creation from external SAML IdPs can fail unless required fields are mapped from IdP attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure required attributes such as email, first name, and last name are available/mapped, or else SAML login failures are setup failures rather than security rejections.

For I4 email/account-linking tests, ZITADEL supports automatic creation, automatic update, manual creation, manual linking, and automatic linking options on external IdPs. The fuzzer MUST control these options during provider setup; otherwise identity merges or prompts may be by-design account-linking behavior rather than a principal-binding flaw.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish between explicit/manual linking flows and automatic linking behavior. If automatic linking options are enabled, account linking based on configured criteria may be by design; tests must specifically verify whether unverified email alone causes linking without the intended policy.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. The fuzzer MUST first mint subject/actor tokens containing both candidate audiences when testing wrong-audience enforcement; otherwise rejection is expected setup behavior, not evidence of correct or incorrect audience validation logic.

For I5 token exchange scope escalation tests, ZITADEL allows scope to differ from the supplied token and can extend or decrease scope, but invalid or excessive scope yields invalid_scope. The fuzzer MUST compare granted claims/scope in the exchanged token against upstream authorization and requested scope, not assume any scope change is a violation.

For I5 token exchange resource tests, the resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource-based token exchange outcomes as evidence of authorization binding behavior on ZITADEL.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT profile or private_key_jwt client assertions, the JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls. Failures outside this window are expected setup failures, not freshness enforcement findings on the target token under test.

For OIDC nonce-related tests in brokered flows, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and is echoed into the ID token when provided. The fuzzer MUST include and track nonce when using implicit/hybrid-style checks; missing nonce in such flows is invalid setup, not a broker vulnerability.

ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default. The fuzzer SHOULD prefer introspection or userinfo for verification rather than local JWT parsing unless the application/token exchange explicitly requested JWT access tokens.

The revocation endpoint revokes access_token or refresh_token granted to the client. The fuzzer MUST authenticate revocation requests as the proper client and must not assume revocation semantics for unrelated clients or audiences.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the service-provider flow first and obtain a SAML request/intent before attempting saml_login; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For SAML login on ZITADEL, the executor MUST preserve and bind the exact SAML request context (including request ID / InResponseTo and RelayState) from the initiated SP flow. Sending a fabricated standalone SAMLResponse without matching request context will be rejected for flow reasons, not necessarily because signature or issuer checks worked.

SAML SSO endpoint /saml/v2/SSO returns HTTP 200 even on protocol errors; failures are encoded inside the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from the SAML endpoint as success. Success/failure must be determined from the downstream OIDC/token completion or parsed SAML status, otherwise I1/I2/I5 tests will false-positive.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, ZITADEL documentation explicitly states the SP/ACS must validate signatures and parties, but the public docs here do not expose per-provider flags like validateSignature or wantAssertionsSigned. The fuzzer MUST test by observing acceptance/rejection behavior of forged assertions, not by assuming configurable enforcement knobs are available via documented API.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, issuer/entity ID trust is established from exchanged metadata between ZITADEL and the external SAML IdP. The fuzzer MUST configure the provider with real metadata first, then mutate only the assertion Issuer during login. Otherwise a failure may be caused by missing provider trust setup rather than issuer validation.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a CONTROL login with a valid assertion in the same SP-initiated flow setup before sending the expired assertion. Otherwise LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from invalid SAML request context or missing attribute mapping.

ZITADEL user creation from external SAML IdPs can fail unless required attributes are mapped via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure required fields (for example email, first name, last name, username/IdP link) are populated during SAML broker login, or authentication failures may be onboarding failures rather than security rejections.

For I4 email-binding and account-linking tests, ZITADEL supports automatic creation, automatic update, manual creation, manual linking, and automatic linking options for external IdPs. The fuzzer MUST control these linking/creation settings during setup; otherwise identity merges may be by-design account linking rather than principal-binding failures.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, ZITADEL documentation indicates external IdP profile fields can be set by actions, including setEmailVerified(boolean). The fuzzer MUST explicitly drive email_verified=false in the external identity data path when testing unverified-email linking; otherwise a verified email may legitimately link or create accounts.

If organization-specific login settings override instance defaults, the OIDC authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} to select the intended organization and its external IdP configuration. Without this scope, tests may hit default settings and the wrong IdP/policy, causing false results in SAML broker scenarios.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the authenticating user is a member of the selected organization. Unknown organizations fail, and non-membership blocks login. Multi-tenant tests MUST account for this membership gate when interpreting login failures.

Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST use an introspection client/application that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false can be caused by audience mismatch rather than token invalidity or revocation.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, ZITADEL enforces that requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. The fuzzer MUST first mint subject/actor tokens with the relevant project audience scopes, then request a narrowed audience. A request for a new audience outside the combined set is expected to fail by design.

For I5 token exchange scope tests, ZITADEL allows scope to differ from the supplied token and can extend or decrease scope, but invalid or excessive scope yields invalid_scope. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token claims against upstream authorization and requested scope carefully; broader scope may be by configured token-exchange behavior, while claims beyond authorized scope are the actual violation target.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 bearer grant profile as a token grant. Do NOT model SAML broker login as POST /oauth/v2/token with a SAML assertion. SAML-relevant testing on this platform is browser/SP-initiated SAML brokering followed by OIDC token issuance.
For OIDC callback validation after SAML brokering, session_token MUST be the access_token, not the id_token. UserInfo and API verification calls require the access token as Bearer credential.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT-based grants or client assertions, JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use claim templates relative to now (for example iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}) for controls; otherwise failures may be due to malformed client assertion/JWT profile setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For token exchange using requested_token_type=id_token, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token field as a Bearer API credential in this mode.
Token exchange does not support resource indicators on ZITADEL. Supplying resource is expected to fail with invalid_target and must not be interpreted as an authorization-binding bug.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens even when used as subject_token in token exchange. Freshness tests using expired subject ID tokens should expect rejection by design and must not be reported as replay-only behavior.

When using token exchange impersonation, actor_token is optional in general but required for impersonation cases using subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt or urn:zitadel:params:oauth:token-type:user_id. Sending only a self-signed JWT or only a user ID as subject_token is expected to fail.
ZITADEL access tokens are opaque by default. The fuzzer SHOULD prefer introspection or userinfo for verification rather than assuming local JWT parsing will work on every access token.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
